meta.title: Universal Paperclips — Speedrun Bot
meta.subtitle: Scoping & planning
meta.headline: Let’s lock the plan for the bot.
meta.lede: Research is done — I dissected the game’s actual source (main.js, projects.js, combat.js) and the community’s speedrun wisdom. Below are the decisions that finalize the build. **Each is pre-filled with my recommended default and the reasoning behind it.** Your job is just to review, override where you have a view, and flag anything you want to talk through.
steps: I return the phased plan + MVP spec

constraints.label: Legit play
constraints.text: read state, act via real controls

context.title: Project context — the game, the proposed phases, and the architecture
context.note: The game is three stages selected by two flags (`humanFlag`, `spaceFlag`). The run’s timer stop is “Universal Paperclips achieved” (`clips ≥ 3e55`); your chosen goal plays past it into the ending fork.

cards.title: Stage 1 · Business
cards.body: Make & sell clips → autoclippers, wire economy, price/marketing. Trust → processors/memory → ops → projects; investments & tournaments fund it; quantum computing.

cards.title: Stage 2 · Space
cards.body: Consume Earth with drones/factories + power/swarm, then Space Exploration → von Neumann probes (8 trust sliders) that self-replicate, explore, harvest & fight drifters.

cards.title: Stage 3 · Endgame
cards.body: Emperor-of-Drift dialogue, the Accept vs Reject choice, then dismantle / prestige restart / heat-death credits.

items.desc: **Foundations** — repo, esbuild bundle, `game.d.ts`, empty 3-layer skeleton, Config type
**MVP** — Stage-1 opener end-to-end: sim + bot + telemetry reach first Trust milestones & first project, with matching splits
**Finish Stage 1** — investments, tournaments, quantum → Release the HypnoDrones
**Stage 2a** — Earth conversion: drones, factories, power, swarm → Space Exploration
**Stage 2b/3** — probes, drift, combat proxy → “achieved” (true-ending goal met)
**Ending fork + optimizer** — play to a terminal ending; full-run Config search
**Hardening** — robustness, fidelity audit, userscript packaging, WR target

blocks.heading: Shared-core architecture
lines: ~Layer 1 — Game-model core~ (pure TS, 100 Hz, seeded RNG) · sim of every mechanic
~Layer 2 — Strategy~ (one **Config** + rule modules + stage state machine) · **byte-identical offline & live**
~Layer 3 — Adapters~ · SIM (drives core, headless)  |  LIVE (reads real globals, clicks real controls)

questions.question: Primary optimization metric?
questions.why: The leaderboard moved IGT → RTA because in-game time is browser-speed-gamable; RTA is the honest speedrun metric. (d) is cheap insurance.

options.label: Real wall-clock (RTA) to “achieved”
options.detail: Time from run start to “Universal Paperclips achieved” (milestone 14→15). The honest speedrun metric.

options.label: In-game time (IGT)
options.detail: ticks/100. Simple, but gamable by browser speed.

options.label: RTA through a chosen ending
options.detail: Keep the clock running past the timer stop, all the way to Accept/Reject.

options.label: Track both RTA + IGT

questions.question: “True ending” scope — where does the run officially end?
questions.why: Your stated goal is “reach the true ending (all 3 stages),” which implies playing past the Any% timer into the ending fork. The optimized-metric window (Q1) can still end at “achieved.”

options.label: Stop at “achieved”
options.detail: All matter converted; everything after is optional.

options.label: Through the full endgame to a terminal ending
options.detail: Reach Accept (project147) or Reject (project148) + its terminal state (prestige restart, or Quantum Temporal Reversion).

options.label: Reject → heat-death credits specifically

questions.question: Is speeding up the game’s own tick rate in scope?
questions.why: The sim is an offline model where wall-clock doesn’t matter, so it should run as fast as the CPU allows; tampering with the live clock is the IGT exploit and breaks legit-play RTA.

options.label: Sim: yes (headless, as fast as CPU). Live bot: no
options.detail: Live stays 100 Hz nominal, tab foregrounded, no timer tampering.

options.label: Both may accelerate ticks
options.detail: Treat tick manipulation as legit for the live run too.

options.label: Neither — both pinned to 100 Hz real-time

questions.question: Target platform for the live bot?
questions.why: The in-page TypeScript + console/userscript delivery is a desktop workflow; mobile is reportedly ~4× faster but a separate build target.

options.label: Desktop
Mobile
Both
options.detail: Desktop first, mobile as a second target.

questions.question: Overall simulator fidelity target?
questions.why: Tuning is only trustworthy if the sim matches the game — the whole point of “validate the bot against the live site.” (c) is the pragmatic fallback given the combat question (Q7).

options.label: Tick-exact deterministic core (100 Hz), seeded RNG
options.detail: Reproduce production, ops, trust, demand/sales, wire price, investment, tournaments, drones, probes within float tolerance.

options.label: Coarse / analytic model
options.detail: Closed-form rates per phase, no per-tick RNG. Fast but approximate.

options.label: Hybrid: tick-exact Stages 1–2, analytic Stage-3 combat only
options.detail: Exact where it matters, proxy for the boids combat.

questions.question: How to model stochastic subsystems (wire price, sales, investment, tournament grids)?
questions.why: (c) both modes is arguably ideal — EV mode makes the tuning search fast and smooth, seeded mode validates fidelity. If forced to one, (a) preserves faithfulness. Switch to (c) if you want both.

options.label: Seeded PRNG with the same call sites as source
options.detail: Expose the seed for reproducible runs; faithful to the game.

options.label: Expected-value / deterministic approximation
options.detail: Replace random gates with their means.

options.label: Both modes, switchable
options.detail: EV for fast search, seeded for validation.

questions.question: How should combat be modeled?
questions.why: The shipped combat is a 60 fps canvas boids sim with per-cell dice; the closed-form formula is dead code. Full boids is expensive and combat is a late, bounded concern.

options.label: Analytic proxy
options.detail: Model net probe/drifter attrition per battle from force ratio + probeCombat·0.15 vs 1.75 + OODA, calibrated on a few live battles; accept honor divergence.

options.label: Faithful boids reproduction
options.detail: Grid, flocking, RNG — exact but heavy and hard to validate.

options.label: Black box
options.detail: Live bot just reacts (raise Combat when drifters>1M); sim approximates honor/loss with a tunable constant.

questions.question: How faithfully to model background-tab throttling / loop drift?
questions.why: Modeling throttle adds noise to tuning; better to keep the sim ideal and measure the live gap.

options.label: Sim assumes ideal 100 Hz; live bot measures actual tick rate as telemetry
options.detail: Explains sim-vs-live divergence without polluting tuning.

options.label: Model a throttling factor in the sim too
Ignore entirely

questions.question: Confirm the “model exactly” vs “approximate” split.
questions.why: (a) matches where fidelity actually affects strategy; (c) is a reasonable MVP-scoping compromise (see Q20).

options.label: Exact economy/ops/trust/creativity/sales/costs/quantum/investment/tournament/drones/factories/power/probes/drift; approximate boids combat, wire-price RNG timing, swarm-gift micro-timing
options.detail: The split that tracks where fidelity affects strategy.

options.label: Everything exact, including combat + wire RNG
Only Stage 1 exact for MVP; Stages 2–3 approximate initially

questions.question: Decision-engine style?
questions.why: (a) is the synthesized best practice — modular rules toggle on/off for A/B tuning and map cleanly to phases. (b) is a strong later upgrade for project sequencing.

options.label: Ordered rule array per concern + stage state machine, on a shared Config
options.detail: Modular, toggle-able rules; the recommended structure.

options.label: Scored-priority policy (utility maximization)
options.detail: Score over active projects + resource actions.

options.label: Monolithic sequential if-loop

questions.question: Config format & how strategy is parameterized?
questions.why: (a) guarantees the sim and live bot run identical parameters — the core validation premise. (c) is a nice add-on for live tweaking.

options.label: Single typed Config object; literal defaults, JSON-overridable
options.detail: Same object consumed by sim and live bot.

options.label: External JSON/YAML file only
UI-editable live panel that mutates Config

questions.question: How are project purchases decided?
questions.why: Projects have no callable handler — the bot clicks #projectButtonN. A scored list is flexible and tunable; a fixed sequence is brittle to RNG-driven timing.

options.label: Scored priority list over activeProjects
options.detail: Weight × affordability × phase-relevance; buy highest-scoring affordable project each tick. Skip-list = negative weights.

options.label: Hard-coded ordered sequence per stage
Buy-everything-affordable (greedy) minus a skip-list
options.detail: Skip AutoTourney, OODA, Glory, late Threnody.

questions.question: How does the bot drive select / slider controls?
questions.why: The game polls sliderPos/riskiness/pick from element values every 100 ms, so setting the value is sufficient and legit.

options.label: Set element value / selectedIndex; let the 100 ms poll pick it up
options.detail: Matches how the game reads controls.

options.label: Dispatch synthetic input events
options.detail: Alternative if a control needs an event.

options.label: Call underlying raise/lowerProbe* handlers for sliders; set .value for selects
options.detail: Clean path for probe sliders (they are +/- handlers).

questions.question: Use the tournament read-winner exploit?
questions.why: It uses only permitted actions (reads state, sets the real control) and is a big yomi multiplier: run the tourney, read the live winner, set the dropdown to it before declareWinner reads it → max beatBoost + podium bonus.

options.label: Yes — it’s legit play and materially boosts yomi
options.detail: Reads state, sets the real control.

options.label: No — pick GREEDY up front, accept the outcome
Configurable (default on)

questions.question: What live surface does the bot expose?
questions.why: (a) is the essential minimum and cheap; (c) is the stretch once the pipeline exists.

options.label: In-page overlay div + window.__botTelemetry export
options.detail: Phase, RTA/IGT clock, key rates, last N decisions, next target.

options.label: Console logging only
Overlay + live sparkline charts

questions.question: What to capture per run?
questions.why: (a) bounds memory while keeping the audit trail needed to explain slow runs and diff against the sim. Splits are the speedrun scoreboard.

options.label: Throttled ring buffer (1–4 Hz) + milestone splits + decision log
options.detail: Core stocks/rates + split timestamps + (rule, tick, state delta, cost).

options.label: Milestone splits only
Everything every tick

questions.question: Which milestone splits to timestamp?
questions.why: (a) is the standard granularity for locating where a run loses time; per-project timestamps come free from the decision log.

options.label: Full set
options.detail: first autoclipper, investmentEngineFlag, strategyEngineFlag, first project, Creativity, each Trust milestone, qFlag, 100 Trust / Release, spaceFlag, first probe, battleFlag, swarm online, “achieved,” each endTimer.

options.label: Just the 3 stage transitions + finish
Full set + per-project purchase timestamps

questions.question: Run comparison / persistence?
questions.why: (a) is the classic scoreboard; (c) is the high-value validation loop and should follow soon.

options.label: Persist each run to localStorage + downloadable JSON; compare via split table + overlaid curves
In-memory only for the session
(a) + automatic live-vs-sim trajectory diff

questions.question: How is the bot validated against the live site?
questions.why: (a) is the practical continuous check; (c) is the gold standard once seeded RNG (Q6) exists.

options.label: Same Config + same decision code run in sim and in-page; assert splits + trajectories match
Manual spot-checks of a few live runs vs sim
Capture a live run’s telemetry, replay its RNG/decisions in the sim, diff

questions.question: MVP stage boundary — smallest end-to-end slice?
questions.why: (a) is the true minimum that exercises the full architecture (production, sales, cost curves, trust→ops, one project, telemetry, sim parity) without the heavy investment/tournament/space systems.

options.label: Stage 1 only, up to first Trust milestones + first project purchase
options.detail: Proves sim + bot + telemetry + Config on the earliest mechanics.

options.label: All of Stage 1 through Release the HypnoDrones
A vertical slice touching all 3 stages shallowly

questions.question: Live-bot delivery format?
questions.why: (a) covers both distribution and is the recommended path; (c) is a dev-loop convenience layer.

options.label: esbuild → single IIFE bundle (console paste + userscript)
Console-paste only
Bookmarklet / loader injecting a locally-served bundle

questions.question: Where does the simulator run?
questions.why: (a) enables fast parameter search; sharing the core with the in-page bot (c) is the ideal end-state but Node-first is simpler to start.

options.label: Node / headless (TypeScript, shared core)
In-browser worker
Both (shared core compiled for Node + browser)

questions.question: Shared-core structure between sim and bot?
questions.why: (a) maximizes reuse and guarantees the strategy that tunes offline is the code that runs live — the core validation premise.

options.label: Three layers: game-model core · strategy/Config · adapters (sim + live)
Separate codebases with a shared Config schema only
Bot only; sim is a throwaway script

questions.question: Tuning / search method for the simulator?
questions.why: (a) is pragmatic — get parity first, then optimize; community priors seed the initial grid.

options.label: Manual sweeps + grid search first; add an optimizer later
options.detail: random / CMA-ES / hill-climb once parity holds.

options.label: Full black-box optimizer from day one
Hand-tuning only

questions.question: operations vs standardOps negative-drift quirk.
questions.why: Tournaments/projects gate on operations but spend standardOps; a tempOps-funded tournament can push standardOps negative. Faithful sim + conservative bot avoids surprise negative-ops states.

options.label: Reproduce faithfully in the sim; bot avoids it (spend only when standardOps ≥ cost)
Reproduce and let the bot exploit / ignore it
Ignore in the sim (approximate ops as one pool)

questions.question: Combat proxy calibration data.
questions.why: Empirical calibration is far more reliable than reverse-engineering the boids stochastics.

options.label: Capture 3–5 live battles’ probe/drifter/honor deltas to fit the proxy
Derive the proxy purely from the boids code by reasoning
Defer combat tuning; use a conservative fixed combat allocation

questions.question: Optimal tournament pick ranking.
questions.why: GREEDY is the reasoned best but unproven vs A100/B100 over random grids; (c) largely moots this if the read-winner exploit is on.

options.label: Monte-Carlo the 8 strategies over many random grids in the sim; default GREEDY until proven
Assume GREEDY, don’t verify
Always use the read-winner exploit (Q14), so pick ranking is moot

questions.question: Probe-trust allocation optimum.
questions.why: Community heuristics disagree; the replication-vs-drift-vs-combat-vs-exploration trade is unsolved — exactly what the sim is for. (c) is a good live shape whose setpoints the sim tunes.

options.label: Treat as a sim optimization; parameterize allocation in Config, seed with Zurd’s heuristic
options.detail: Let offline search find the fastest 3e55 conversion.

options.label: Hard-code one community heuristic
options.detail: Zurd: Haz5 + Self-Rep + Combat-in-war; or fandom: Haz6 + ≥4 Self-Rep.

options.label: Dynamic feedback controller
options.detail: Raise Self-Rep while clips surplus, raise Combat while drifters>1M.

questions.question: Reference WR / target time.
questions.why: The record is motivational, not a build dependency; verifying it needs a manual browser visit (speedrun.com blocks fetch).

options.label: Don’t gate the build on it; set an internal target, verify records live later
options.detail: e.g. beat casual ~1–2 h, then chase ~1h30m desktop.

options.label: Manually fetch / confirm the current WR before starting
Ignore records entirely; optimize against our own best

questions.question: Swarm-slider (Think ↔ Work) target policy.
questions.why: Work maximizes throughput, Think maximizes free processor/memory gifts; a scheduled crossover matches the observed optimal shape and is tunable.

options.label: Config-parameterized schedule (Work-heavy consuming Earth, Think-heavy near the end); sim tunes the crossover
Fixed value (community ~150)
Closed-loop on whether ops/memory is the bottleneck

questions.question: Save-management policy for the live bot.
questions.why: Autosave is every 25 s; letting it run protects against crashes without interfering.

options.label: Let the game autosave; optionally save() after major purchases; never touch savePrestige unless intended
Disable / ignore saves entirely (fresh run each time)
Snapshot state to __botTelemetry independent of the game’s save
